item.title: PIBT*_T Enables Fast Turn‑Aware Path Planning for Hundreds of Mobile Robots
item.description:
PIBT*_T Enables Fast Turn‑Aware Path Planning for Hundreds of Mobile Robots

A new algorithm, PIBT*_T, accelerates multi‑agent path planning by handling turn actions explicitly.

🔍 Overview

  • Large‑scale multi‑mobile‑robot systems require fast and reliable path planning under realistic motion constraints.
  • MAPF_T explicitly models orientation changes and turn‑induced delays, but these constraints increase the computational burden of search‑based methods.
  • Priority‑inheritance‑based planning offers a highly scalable alternative, yet directly extending it to MAPF_T is nontrivial because turn actions break the immediate node‑vacation assumption underlying conventional priority inheritance.

🧩 How it Works

  • PIBT*_T is an efficient iterative solver for MAPF_T.
  • It preserves the lightweight single‑timestep planning mechanism of Priority Inheritance with Backtracking (PIBT) while introducing dedicated mechanisms to handle:
    • Turn‑induced dependencies
    • Local deadlocks
    • Livelock
    • Inefficient repeated pushing

⚙️ Key Details

  • Experiments on standard MAPF benchmarks show that PIBT*_T achieves high success rates and strong scalability, solving instances with up to 1000 agents within seconds.
  • For realistic engineering environments, Action Dependency Graph (ADG)-based execution simulation and a flexible manufacturing system case study demonstrate that turn‑aware planning better reflects robot execution and reduces actual makespan compared with classical MAPF planning.
  • Experiments with TurtleBot4 robots further validate the practical feasibility of the proposed method.

💡 Why it Matters

  • Enables scalable coordination of hundreds of robots by explicitly modeling turns.
  • Improves real‑world execution efficiency through accurate turn‑aware planning.
  • Shows that priority‑inheritance techniques can be extended to complex action models without sacrificing scalability.

#MultiAgentPathFinding #Robotics #PriorityInheritance #TurtleBot #ADG

Source: Scalable Iterative Multi-Agent Path Finding under Turn Constraints

item.title: Goal-Branching LaCAM Improves Dense Multi-Agent Pathfinding
item.description:
Goal-Branching LaCAM Improves Dense Multi-Agent Pathfinding

Goal-Branching LaCAM introduces temporary goals to help a multi‑agent pathfinding solver handle dense, corridor‑heavy environments.

🔍 Overview

  • LaCAM is a search‑based solver for Multi‑Agent Pathfinding (MAPF) that performs a depth‑first search over joint configurations.
  • It uses PIBT (Priority Inheritance with Backtracking) to generate successors and lazily adds single‑agent constraints to explore alternatives.
  • While complete, LaCAM struggles on dense maps because deadlocks often require coordinated moves of several agents away from their goals, which PIBT’s greedy one‑step successors rarely propose.

🧩 How Goal‑Branching Works

  • The paper proposes Goal‑Branching, where blocking agents receive temporary goals.
  • Each temporary goal is explored as an additional branch of LaCAM’s search.
  • Random and corridor‑aware rules are examined for selecting these temporary goals.
  • Completeness is preserved for any such rule.

⚙️ Key Results

Metric Goal‑Branching LaCAM LaCAM*
Solve rate on dense instances (60‑90% occupancy) 89% 44%
First‑solution speedup on maze‑32‑32‑2 and room‑32‑32‑4 (instances both solve) 10‑14× faster Baseline
Median time speedup at 75% density on room‑32‑32‑4 ~200× faster Baseline
Solution cost increase on instances both solve 15‑22% higher Baseline
Solution cost on open maps and full MovingAI benchmark No higher than LaCAM* (≤3% slower) Baseline

💡 Why It Matters

  • By adding temporary goals, the solver can break deadlocks without enumerating constraints agent by agent.
  • The approach retains the completeness of the original algorithm while dramatically improving success rates and runtime on challenging dense maps.
  • Cost overhead is modest and disappears on less congested environments.

Submitted on 5 Nov 2026

#MultiAgentPathfinding #AIPlanning #GoalBranching

Source: Goal-Branching LaCAM: Temporary Goals as Search Branches in Dense Multi-Agent Pathfinding
